claims.claim: The micro:bit Think→Create→Evaluate→Extend→Share lesson arc embeds formative assessment in the Evaluate and Share phases, so a single 45-60 min MakeCode block session should treat assessment as embedded demos/reflections, not a bolted-on written test.

Demo-based checks (student holds up the running micro:bit so the teacher sees the LED output, animation, or gesture response) are the most natural lightweight formative check because the board's physical behaviour is directly observable without any writing.

Exit-ticket questions can be delivered orally or visually (e.g. 'point to the block that makes it repeat forever') instead of written, which fits pre-literate or early-literate kids within one 45-60 min block session.
Peer-share prompts (pairs compare what their badge/sprite/program does) slot into the Share phase and let one teacher overhear-check several students at once at near-zero prep cost.

L1-s4 (step counter) and L1-s6 (rock-paper-scissors) upstream microbit.org lessons carried structured teacher assessment and success criteria that were dropped in repackaging, so they should be re-inserted as non-written demo/success-criteria checks rather than reinvented.

A single 45-60 min session should cap formative assessment at one quick Evaluate check plus one Share share (no multi-question quiz) to protect MakeCode building time, per the one-idea-per-slide pedagogy constraint.
